chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding the man who buys a boy or a girl, and for him is a brother or a sister or a father or a mother in a city from the cities. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not send him to another city if he is young, and do not buy him. So if he has a mother, and she is pleased and he is pleased, then buy him if you wish.'

key_terms.فَطَابَتْ نَفْسُهَا وَ نَفْسُهُ: she and he were both pleased/content

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on separating a slave from their family members in another city?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizing the preservation of *silat al-rahim* (kinship ties) as a primary legal consideration in manumission and ownership transactions. The hadith establishes a default prohibition against separating young slaves from their close relatives in other cities, reflecting the Shia emphasis on family cohesion, while providing a pragmatic exception based on mutual consent (*taradhin*) between the mother and the child. This ruling illustrates the juristic balance between property rights and the spiritual merit of maintaining familial bonds.
